Applying the time-dependent jump generator to X_t A_t gives an exact closed pair for w=E[A_t^2] and c=E[X_t A_t]: w'=2c, c'=D/mu-(mu+r)c+r w/t. Laplace transform with w(0)=w'(0)=0, w(t)<=D t^2/mu, yields a unique transform, an exact hypergeometric inversion and a critical exponential-integral limit. Standard asymptotics for {}_1F_1 prove the three stated powers and constants; separate numerical ODE and quadrature checks pass 233 assertions.

originality.rationale: The 2024 motivating article evaluates one-time marginal spectral relaxation and equilibrium Gibbs densities. The new path-integral observable requires a two-time moment identity absent from those inspected sections; its sharp empirical-mean variance threshold and finite-T Kummer formula are not consequences of a one-time position law. The 2016/2017 work is unconfined and concerns position spreading; the 2025 extension treats memory-kernel-dependent marginal relaxation. Search and full-text comparisons find no covering statement, with explicit residual risk from general reinforced-process theory.
residual_risks: An equivalently strong general central-limit, urn, or stochastic-approximation theorem could imply the piecewise exponent without matching the model name.
A missed article on empirical means of reinforced confined random walks could contain the same formula or stronger results.
Full analysis here is confined to Gaussian harmonic equilibrium start and uniform lookback; no distributional or almost-sure limit established.

value.rationale: Finite-window averaging is an experimentally and mathematically natural way to estimate equilibrium position from a single trajectory. The result reveals a rate threshold invisible in all instantaneous Gibbs marginals: ordinary inverse-time precision for r<mu, a logarithmic slowdown at r=mu, and nonstandard T^{-2mu/(mu+r)} convergence for r>mu. Exact finite-time coefficients make the transition testable and supply a benchmark for memory-dependent transport; mean-square concentration still holds.
